title: Tio's symphony band and getting fired as a snake charmer
summary: Tio asked what music he wanted to play; Bigard said jazz, though playing in Tio's club symphony band helped his reading, and at a club job near Oswego the boss fired him for holding one note.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And that's how the thing went on. And when he said, "Well, now, son, I've taught you." He says, "I

know you want to go out and play music if you feel like it. What kind do you want to play?" And I told him, "I liked the jazz, that fancy music." And we used to have -- he had a band at the club they belonged to like a little symphony band, you know. The old man, and he was the conductor and he used to ask me to come and sit and play with them.

Yeah. But I didn't like that. But it was good for my reading, you know. But then when I went to go to play jazz then it was a different story altogether. I had to divide my music, what I had learned. I had to divide the time, the tempo, and I was getting kind of disgusted, but then I kept at it. I really kept at it for a while.

Then I went, I got a job with some guy in -- he had a job around Oswego somewhere in some kind of club. So one night the boss came in and says, "Where's that damn snake charmer?" And say, "There's no snake charmer here." He says, "I hear that one note. Who's holding that damn one note in my place here?" So he told the guy, "Get rid of him."
So I was fired that night, bam, and I said, "Oh, well."
